newsitem.title: USA: LDC debts on bull run, key Bradies make year high.
newsitem.headline: LDC debts on bull run, key Bradies make year high.

text.p: Major Brady bonds hit new highs of the year on Monday, showing no fatigue after last week's rally.
"It's part of the global asset rally," said the head trader of emerging market debts at an investment bank.
Among star performers, Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR jumped 1-5/8 to 83-5/8. Brazil C BR8D14=RR rose 7/8 to 69-1/2, Venezuela DCBs VZFLL07=RR gained 7/8 to 81-1/2.
But some traders warned that the "yield compression" of the Bradies is close to the level seen just before the peso crisis in January 1994.
They said the breathless rally masked divergent views of the market direction, and warned that some of the factors that underpin the present market could be temporary.

"The market is not prepared for the next FOMC meeting," said one U.S. bank trader. Recent data suggesting a slower U.S. economy have dampened expectations that the Federal Open Market Committee would tighten credit when it meets on September 24.
The trader added that the Brady market's surge has been based largely on rising oil prices which may turn out to be fleeting.
A case in point is Venezuela, whose Bradies rose by leaps and bounds solely on the strength of oil revenues.
Oil revenues account for a larger percentage of gross domestic product for Venezuela than for Mexico, said Carlos Asilis, Latin America economist at Oppenheimer, Inc.
"The international reserves of the country increases at the rate of $150 to 200 million a week, that's very positive for the interest rate," he said.
The rising reserves give Venezuela the wherewithal to defend the currency, he added.
But the oil-inspired optimism may have run ahead of itself, as investors overlooked the challenges on the fiscal side, Asilis said.
Under normal circumstances, it would be difficult to envisage Venezuela papers trading at tigher spreads than Argentine papers, he said.

But the stripped yield spreads have contracted in the rally faster for Venezuela than for Argentina. Traders quoted about 726 basis points for Venezuela PARs VZ675C20=RR, compared to 769 basis points for Argentina Pars AR4C23=RR.
Options traders also noted that divergent views of the market direction are reflected in increased activities in the over-the-counter options.
"Some people try to cut exposure by buying puts or writing covered calls," said an options trader. "But others believe the trend is continuing and add new exposure."
